Define genome effects from coefficients you supply

Source: R/define_genome_effect_terms.R
define_genome_effect_terms.Rd

Writes genome-effect terms whose coefficients you already know (GWAS estimates, a published QTL map, a hand-built test model) for one trait. Each term is one coefficient (genome_effects) over one or more loci (genome_effect_members), each locus optionally restricted to allele copies from a given line and/or parent (genome_effect_member_origins). add_tgv() then evaluates every term into ind_tgv.

Nothing is sampled or scaled: the coefficients are written as given, so the trait has whatever variance they imply. To sample effects calibrated to a target variance use define_additive_effects() or define_genome_effects(). Those generators write the reserved owner "generated" through the same internal engine; this function refuses that owner, so your terms and generated ones never replace each other.

Most models are easiest to build with the helpers, which return terms rows that rbind() together:

  • ad_terms(): additive and dominance coefficients per locus;

  • aa_terms(): additive-by-additive coefficients per locus pair;

  • genotype_terms(): any genotypic value table over one or more loci.

Usage

define_genome_effect_terms(
  pop,
  trait_name,
  terms,
  effect_owner = "custom",
  mode = c("append", "replace_scope", "replace_owner", "replace_trait"),
  origin = NULL,
  base_tbl = NULL,
  require_complete = FALSE
)

Arguments

pop

A tidybreed_pop.

trait_name

Character scalar: an existing trait (from define_trait()).

terms

A data frame of terms; see The terms data frame. Usually built with ad_terms(), aa_terms() and genotype_terms().

effect_owner

Character scalar labelling who owns these terms, so a later call can replace them without touching anyone else's. Owners never compete: all owners' terms add. Default "custom"; "generated" is reserved for the generators and refused.

mode

"append" (default), "replace_scope", "replace_owner" or "replace_trait"; see Replacement modes.

origin

NULL (default, every allele copy), a named list of scalars or a per-member data frame; see Scope (origin).

base_tbl

Optional tidybreed_table from get_table() (optionally filtered) whose allele frequencies fill any missing center_value on additive and dominance members: founder_haplotypes, ind_haplotype, or any table with an id_ind column, from the same pop (see extract_allele_freq()). Given centres are never overwritten, and indicator members have none. NULL (default) fills nothing, so a missing centre is an error. The fill is Cockerham p; functional coding writes 0.5 itself (as ad_terms() does). One call gives one p per locus, so write line-specific terms one line per call.

require_complete

Logical. TRUE requires an indicator table to cover every reachable genotype state of its loci (including copy_count_value = 0 where a chromosome can be absent). Default FALSE: a state you leave out contributes zero.

Value

The tidybreed_pop, invisibly. Run add_tgv() to evaluate the terms; get_table(pop, "genome_effect_terms") lists them.

The terms data frame

One row per (term x locus), the long shape every get_table() table has.

ColumnRequiredMeaning
term_idyes, unless one termGroups rows into one term. Input only: never stored; the writer assigns an id_genome_effect. Any atomic type
genome_valueyesThe term's coefficient. Constant within a term_id
effect_namenoA free label per term (constant within a term_id); no mathematical meaning
locus_nameyesA locus in genome_meta; each locus at most once per term
contrast_nameyes"additive": each counted allele-1 copy minus center_value (g - 2 * center_value over both copies). "dominance": the HWE dominance contrast at center_value. "indicator": 1 when the locus is in the state below, else 0
center_valueadditive, dominanceThe centre: the allele-1 frequency p for Cockerham (statistical) coding, 0.5 for functional coding. May be left NA with base_tbl
copy_count_value, dosage_valueindicatorThe genotype state: copies present and copies of allele 1. copy_count_value may be left NA at ordinary diploid autosomal loci (it is 2)

A term with several members is their product, so a two-locus additive term is an A x A interaction and a two-locus indicator term is one cell of a two-locus genotype table.

Scope (origin)

  • NULL (default): the common scope, every allele copy.

  • A named list of scalars applied to every member of every term, with names among line_name, parent_origin (1 sire, 2 dam), line_match_type and copy_count. list(line_name = "Duroc") is copies from line Duroc (line_match_type = "exact"); list(parent_origin = 1) is copies from the sire, any line (line_match_type = "any").

  • A data frame with columns term_id, locus_name, line_match_type ("exact", "unknown" or "any"), line_name, parent_origin, copy_count: one scope per member, needed for the copy combinations a dominance or indicator member takes, such as reciprocal dominance.

An additive member takes at most one origin row. A dominance or indicator member takes one row per kind of copy, whose copy_counts sum to the state's copy count (2 for dominance), so a scalar list is usually not enough for one; the error names the locus.

Where a copy matches both a line-specific term and a common one in the same family (same trait, owner, loci and contrasts), the more specific term applies to it, not both; terms of different owners always add.

Replacement modes

  • "append" (default): insert; a term with the same family and scope as an existing one is refused.

  • "replace_scope": delete this owner's terms for the trait whose scope equals origin, then insert. Needs origin to be NULL or a scalar list.

  • "replace_owner": delete all of this owner's terms for the trait, then insert.

  • "replace_trait": delete every owner's terms for the trait, then insert. Refused while the trait has generated terms: those are replaced only by re-running a generator, or removed with remove_generated_effects().

Rows are never deleted from the genome-effect tables any other way.

See also

ad_terms(), aa_terms() and genotype_terms() build terms; define_additive_effects() and define_genome_effects() for sampled, calibrated effects; add_tgv().

Examples

set.seed(1)
pop <- open_pop(pop_name = "terms_example", db_name = ":memory:") |>
  define_genome(n_loci = 60, n_chr = 2, chr_len_Mb = 100) |>
  define_founder_haplotypes(n_haplotypes = 100, line_name = "Duroc")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpOJ05Ue/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Opened in-memory population 'terms_example'
#> Defined genome: 60 loci across 2 chromosomes | chr lengths (Mb): all equal to 100 Mb
#>   Tables written: genome_meta, genome_map, ind_haplotype, ind_genotype, ind_crossover, chr_inheritance, chr_recombination, genome_effects, genome_effect_members, genome_effect_member_origins
#>   Views created: genome_effect_terms, genome_effect_loci
#> Generating 100 founder haplotypes (method = "uniform")...
#>   Created founder_haplotypes for line 'Duroc' (100 haplotypes x 60 loci)
pop <- pop |>
  get_table("founder_haplotypes") |>
  add_founders(n_males = 10, n_females = 10, line_name = "Duroc")
#> Added 20 founders (10 males, 10 females) to line 'Duroc'
pop <- define_trait(pop, "ADG")
#> Added trait 'ADG'.

# Additive and dominance effects of two loci, functional coding
# (a = half the homozygote difference, d = heterozygote deviation)
pop <- pop |>
  define_genome_effect_terms("ADG",
    ad_terms(c("Locus_10", "Locus_20"), a = c(0.4, -0.2), d = c(0.1, 0),
             p = c(0.3, 0.5)),
    effect_owner = "qtl_map")
#> Implied genetic mean (functional coding), reported only — written to no table: Locus_10 mu = -0.118; Locus_20 mu =  0.000. Running total over these single-locus main effects: -0.118.
#> Wrote 3 genome-effect terms (3 member rows) for trait 'ADG' under owner 'qtl_map' [append].

# An A x A interaction between them, added under its own owner
pop <- pop |>
  define_genome_effect_terms("ADG",
    aa_terms("Locus_10", "Locus_20", e = 0.05, p_1 = 0.3, p_2 = 0.5),
    effect_owner = "epistasis")
#> Implied genetic mean (functional coding), reported only — written to no table: (Locus_10, Locus_20) mu = 0. Running total over these pairs: 0.
#> Wrote 1 genome-effect term (2 member rows) for trait 'ADG' under owner 'epistasis' [append].

# The same kind of rows written directly: one Cockerham additive term
# whose centre is filled from the founders' allele frequency
pop <- pop |>
  define_genome_effect_terms("ADG",
    data.frame(locus_name = "Locus_30", contrast_name = "additive",
               genome_value = 0.25),
    effect_owner = "candidate_gene",
    base_tbl = get_table(pop, "founder_haplotypes"))
#> Wrote 1 genome-effect term (1 member rows) for trait 'ADG' under owner 'candidate_gene' [append].

# An effect only on copies inherited from the sire (imprinting)
pop <- pop |>
  define_genome_effect_terms("ADG",
    ad_terms("Locus_40", a = 0.3, p = 0.5),
    effect_owner = "imprinted", origin = list(parent_origin = 1))
#> Implied genetic mean (functional coding), reported only — written to no table: Locus_40 mu = 0. Running total over these single-locus main effects: 0.
#> Wrote 1 genome-effect term (1 member rows) for trait 'ADG' under owner 'imprinted' [append].

# Reciprocal dominance: the heterozygote value depends on which parent
# gave the Duroc copy and which the Landrace copy
pop <- pop |>
  define_genome_effect_terms("ADG",
    terms = data.frame(term_id = 1L, locus_name = "Locus_50",
                       contrast_name = "dominance", center_value = 0.5,
                       genome_value = 1.2),
    origin = data.frame(term_id = 1L, locus_name = "Locus_50",
                        line_match_type = "exact",
                        line_name = c("Duroc", "Landrace"),
                        parent_origin = c(1L, 2L), copy_count = 1L),
    effect_owner = "reciprocal")
#> Wrote 1 genome-effect term (1 member rows) for trait 'ADG' under owner 'reciprocal' [append].

# Change your mind: replace everything under one owner
pop <- pop |>
  define_genome_effect_terms("ADG",
    ad_terms(c("Locus_10", "Locus_20"), a = c(0.5, -0.1), p = c(0.3, 0.5)),
    effect_owner = "qtl_map", mode = "replace_owner")
#> Implied genetic mean (functional coding), reported only — written to no table: Locus_10 mu = -0.2; Locus_20 mu =  0.0. Running total over these single-locus main effects: -0.2.
#> Wrote 2 genome-effect terms (2 member rows) for trait 'ADG' under owner 'qtl_map' [replace_owner].

get_table(pop, "genome_effect_terms")
#> <tidybreed_table: genome_effect_terms>  [6 rows × 9 fields]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 9
#>   trait_name effect_owner   effect_name id_genome_effect effect_order
#>   <chr>      <chr>          <chr>                  <int>        <dbl>
#> 1 ADG        imprinted      NA                         6            1
#> 2 ADG        reciprocal     NA                         7            1
#> 3 ADG        epistasis      NA                         4            2
#> 4 ADG        candidate_gene NA                         5            1
#> 5 ADG        qtl_map        NA                         8            1
#> 6 ADG        qtl_map        NA                         9            1
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: contrast_signature <chr>, family_key <chr>,
#> #   scope_description <chr>, genome_value <dbl>
pop <- pop |> get_table("ind_meta") |> add_tgv("ADG")
#> Computed TGV for 20 individuals on trait 'ADG' (additive, interaction).
close_pop(pop)
